## Why "Constant a" Is Not Optional

<!-- STEP id="the-picture" -->
The kinematic equations were derived from one picture: a velocity-time graph that is a **straight line** — constant slope, constant acceleration.

<!-- STEP id="the-real-curve" -->
When acceleration ramps up instead, the real velocity-time graph **curves** — flatter at first, steepening as the motor spools up.

<!-- STEP id="smaller-area" -->
The real area under that curve (the true distance) is smaller than the triangle you'd get by assuming $a = 4$ m/s² throughout — because for most of those 4 seconds, the drone's true acceleration was less than 4 m/s².

<!-- STEP id="the-takeaway" -->
**Using a value of $a$ that only holds later over-estimates the distance. Constant acceleration isn't a technicality to skim past — it's the one assumption the entire derivation stands on.**
